assignments.task_summary: Implement one repository projection join for the vertical slice that resolves allowed exact audit/source references without dropping unknown outcomes or multiplying events.
Implement the actual API-specific TanStack hook for the reconciled Spring response, including runtime decoding before cache admission and the established key/cancellation policy.
Connect the existing filter editor, fenced-page hook and reusable list into one read-only Support case-history view with safe source-detail entry points.
Implement the vertical slice’s source-open action so it revalidates current case/source authorization instead of trusting an earlier list response.
Author a compact adversarial test matrix for the finished explorer’s list, continuation and source-open entry points, then repair at most one missing guard.
Implement one explicit response/log projection for the Support explorer that keeps necessary event identifiers while rejecting accidental raw entity or exception serialization.
Implement one cold-refresh/deep-link transition for the finished SPA explorer using session bootstrap, server refetch and safe URL filter restoration.
Implement one authorization-loss state transition across the explorer list, selected row, dialog and local filter state without introducing a new polling mechanism.
Implement and test one best-effort analytics boundary around the existing explorer interaction, preserving the approved allowlist and proving it cannot block history use.
Measure request/query/render work for the existing page 1-to-page 2 explorer interaction and test one narrowly justified reduction or retain the baseline.
Implement a small vertical requirement change: apply the already validated half-open UTC date range consistently from URL/filter model through the history query.
Execute one prepared end-to-end Support explorer scenario and author the specified empty-fence boundary assertion, or an equally bounded newly observed defect assertion with an explicit oracle.
Independently reproduce the exact local explorer candidate and author one executable negative check that detects a candidate/fixture mismatch before interpreting smoke results.

Translate an unfamiliar display-only requirement into an executable grouping model: collapse consecutive observations with the same kind, durable operation and exact source reference within one raw page.
Implement one pure grouped-row adapter from day 86’s contract and connect it to the existing shared list without changing the server API or raw pagination.
Author adversarial tests against the independent grouping adapter and repair at most one bounded defect while preserving raw identity and authorization.

Independently diagnose an unfamiliar seeded fault that repeats a history event during a two-page explorer interaction. Build the smallest reproducer, collect discriminating evidence and identify the responsible seam without an implementation hint.
Implement the smallest repair supported by day 89’s actual diagnosis and compare the repaired grouped display with the existing ungrouped baseline on the same raw-event contract.
Complete a timed independent SQL/debugging mock for an authorized case summary, then execute one new counterexample derived from the debrief within the same primary.
Run only the prepared explorer/grouping demonstration and execute a small claim-to-evidence check that rejects unsupported independent-mastery assertions for this candidate.
Author the request-accounting and hard-stop rules for one local owned-history workload runner, then execute its ten-request dry run.
Run the prepared owned-history path and author a receipt that pairs client durations with server work and failure counts for three bounded trials.
Capture an actual CPU recording for a synthetic repeated-formatting history projection and identify one candidate hotspot with a falsifiable call-path hypothesis.
Use allocation and garbage-collection observations to compare a prepared retain-all projection with its bounded-page input, without changing application behavior yet.
Reconstruct the baseline measurement with recording disabled and enabled under matched conditions, then quantify the uncertainty introduced by profiling.
Implement one bounded projection change suggested by the allocation evidence and compare it with the retained baseline using the same fixture.
Implement resource lifetime handling for one existing read adapter using an instrumented AutoCloseable cursor and a mapping failure.
Diagnose three prepared thread-state samples by capturing actual recordings while a history adapter computes, waits on a barrier or waits for a pooled permit.
Implement one deadline-aware history adapter boundary that cancels unfinished read work and preserves cleanup on timeout.
Reproduce a disclosed shared-monitor contention mechanism and independently author a minimal experiment and one synchronization repair.
Replace one mutable shared formatting snapshot with a safely published immutable snapshot and test a concurrent configuration swap.
Implement bounded admission for the read-only projection executor and expose a safe overload result without running rejected work on the request thread.
Implement one composite read that shares a deadline across two independent safe projections and cancels its sibling after a required branch fails.
Implement graceful shutdown for the bounded read executor and observe accepted, queued and newly rejected work at the shutdown boundary.
Author a focused regression matrix that combines deadline expiry, queue rejection and close failure for the existing read adapter.
Rerun only the selected projection change against its baseline and execute a counterexample that challenges the explanation for the observed result.
Instrument one existing history read boundary to correlate acquisition wait, query duration and request duration using safe request labels.
Configure and test one existing pool acquisition timeout within the request deadline, preserving cleanup and safe failure handling.
Run actual query plans for one active-history predicate under the skewed fixture and compare estimated versus actual cardinality before changing an index.
Implement one bounded history projection that avoids per-row metadata fetches while preserving optional metadata and page cardinality.
Diagnose a seeded read-adapter failure that leaves a transaction resource held, and repair only its transaction/lifetime boundary.
Move one prepared slow mock-provider wait outside the existing SQL transaction while preserving durable intent and atomic result recording.
Create a deterministic two-session reproducer for a supplied opposite lock order in dispatch and cancellation, and classify the database outcome.
Implement a consistent lock order for the two existing competing commands and verify both interleavings against the same fixture.
Implement a bounded whole-transaction retry for one pure database claim path while keeping external calls outside the retried transaction.
Rebuild the owner-scoped fenced history query from its contract without viewing the previous implementation, then execute adversarial cursor cases.
Run a two-session read/update experiment to explain an existing history view snapshot under the installed PostgreSQL isolation level.
Implement and test statement cancellation for one owned read while observing transaction cleanup and subsequent connection reuse.
Connect the existing bounded request-admission seam to pool availability for one read endpoint and measure deliberate rejection versus acquisition waiting.
Compare one existing index with one instructor-prepared candidate index on the same history filter, including a bounded append workload.
